summary: George E. Dunkel is a linguist and Indologist who earned his doctorate from the University of Pennsylvania (~1970–1976). He held posts at Johns Hopkins University (1975–1978), Princeton University (1978–1986), and the University of Zurich (appointed 1986).

George Foot Moore worked in religious studies after studying at Yale (1870–1872) and Union Theological Seminary (~1874–1877). He was a professor at Andover Theological Seminary (1883–1902) and Harvard University, including as Frothingham Professor of the History of Religions (1904–1928).

George Frederick Baumann is an Indologist who completed a PhD at Heidelberg University (~1969–1973) and studied at the Bibliothekar-Lehrinstitut des Landes Nordrhein-Westfalen (~1973–1975). He held posts at the University of Tübingen and its library between ~1975 and 2001.
George Herbert Palmer was a philosopher who attended Phillips Academy (~1858–1860) and Harvard University (~1860–1864). He spent his career on the faculty at Harvard University from ~1870 to 1913.

George L. Hart is an Indologist and linguist who completed a PhD in Sanskrit at Harvard (~1964–1971). He taught Sanskrit at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1969–1975) before serving as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley (~1975–2013).

George Lakoff is a linguist and philosopher who studied at MIT and completed his doctorate at Indiana University Bloomington (~1962–1966). After teaching at Harvard (1965–1969), he served as a professor of linguistics at UC Berkeley from 1972 to 2016.

George Melville Bolling worked in Indology and linguistics after earning a doctorate from Johns Hopkins (~1891–1897). He held professorships at the Catholic University of America (1895–1913) and Ohio State University (1914–1939), and served as president of the Linguistic Society of America (1931).
George R. Elder is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Columbia University, where he was supervised by Alex Wayman (attested 1978).
George Rupp is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Princeton, Yale, and Harvard. He held major posts at Rice University (1985–1993) and Columbia University (~1993–2002).
George Saintsbury studied at King's College School (~1858–1863) and Merton College (~1863–1868). He later held an academic post at the University of Edinburgh from ~1895 to 1915.

Philosopher George Santayana studied at Harvard (PhD ~1886–1890) under William James, with additional studies in Berlin and Cambridge. He later served on Harvard University's philosophy faculty from 1907 to 1912.
George Shirt was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He completed a B.A. at the University of Cambridge by 1864 and studied at the Church Missionary Society College, Islington, from ~1864 to 1866.

Indologist George Thibaut studied under Albrecht Weber in 1867. He served as head of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1875, 1879–1888) and Muir Central College (1888–1895), and worked as registrar at the University of Allahabad (~1887–1895) and the University of Calcutta (~1907–1914).

George Thomas Staunton was a sinologist who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1797–1798). He later served as Vice-President of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland from ~1823 to 1859.

George Turnour worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. He served in the Ceylon Civil Service as a Member of the Supreme Council in 1818 and as Assistant to the Commissioner of Revenue in 1820.

George Uglow Pope worked in Indology and linguistics. He led Breeks Memorial School (1859–1870) and Bishop Cotton Boys' School (1870), and served as Lecturer in Tamil at the University of Oxford from ~1884 to 1908.

George V. Bobrinskoy was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Lutheran Theological Seminary and Yale under Franklin Edgerton. He spent his career at the University of Chicago, serving as assistant professor of Sanskrit (1929–1930) and linguistics department chairman (1951–1966).

George Watt, active in Indology, studied at Aberdeen and Glasgow (M.B. and C.M. ~1871–1873). He was Professor of Botany at Presidency College (1873–1874), served at the University of Calcutta (~1873–1884), and later lectured at the University of Edinburgh (~1907–1909).

George de Roerich worked in Tibetology, Indology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies, studying at London, Harvard, and Paris under scholars including Sylvain Lévi and Charles Rockwell Lanman. He directed the Urusvati Himalayan Research Institute (~1930–1942) and headed a department at the Institute of Oriental Studies (~1957–1960).

George van Driem is a linguist and Tibetologist who studied at Virginia, Nijmegen, and Leiden. He held professorships at Leiden University (1996–1999, ~2001–2009) and served as Professor of Historical Linguistics at the University of Bern (2010–2022).
